summary.intent: Fix a failing lint CI check on PR #455 caused by a pnpm/action-setup upgrade from v5 to v6, then address a Windows build borrow checker error on PR #456, and implement a metadata refresh cleanup bug fix.
summary.outcome: All three issues were resolved: pnpm version pinned via packageManager field, Windows borrow checker error fixed by extracting inode fields before drop, and refreshing_metadata leak fixed by converting PendingRefresh to an enum with Failure variant and extracting a shared spawn_metadata_refresh() helper.

repo: pnpm/action-setup@v6 ignores the `version` input when a `packageManager` field exists in package.json, and can silently install pnpm 11-rc even when `version: 10` is specified — the `packageManager` field takes precedence and is the correct way to pin pnpm version

The codebase uses a PendingContent::Failure / PendingFilePointer::Failure pattern for cleanup on async task error paths — PendingRefresh was missing this pattern and was leaking entries in refreshing_metadata on failure
The shared dir_ops.rs scopes inode borrows inside blocks to drop them before mutable borrows; the Windows-specific dir_ops.rs did not follow this pattern, causing a borrow checker error
pnpm store v10 = pnpm 10, store v11 = pnpm 11 — the store path in CI logs is a reliable signal for which pnpm version is actually running
pnpm 11 treats ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS as a hard error (exit code 1); pnpm 10 only warns

code.finding: inode was borrowed immutably from fs at line 34 and used through line 94, preventing a mutable borrow of fs for refreshing_metadata.insert() at line 62. Fix: extract parent_ino, children, inode_attr from inode then call drop(inode) before the mutable borrow.

drain_refresh_completions() only removed entries from refreshing_metadata on success; failure paths left names stuck permanently blocking future refreshes. Fixed by adding PendingRefresh::Failure variant.

Both needs_refresh and needs_load spawn blocks contained identical resolve/fetch/decrypt logic and both leaked ipns_name in refreshing_metadata on error. Replaced with shared spawn_metadata_refresh() helper.

Async refresh task never removed ipns_name from refreshing_metadata on error paths (resolve, fetch, decrypt failures). Fixed by routing through spawn_metadata_refresh() which sends Failure on all error paths.

workflow: When CI uses a different tool version than local dev, check the store/cache path in logs — it encodes the version (e.g. pnpm store v10 vs v11)

action-setup v6 conflicts with both packageManager field and version input simultaneously — only one source of truth should be used; remove version input from workflow yaml when packageManager is set in package.json
pnpm 11 was pre-release (RC only) at time of session — upgrading the whole project to pnpm 11 was not viable
Worktrees are useful for isolating PR branch work without disrupting the main working directory

friction: action-setup@v6 silently installs pnpm 11-rc despite version: 10 being specified, requiring significant investigation to diagnose via store path forensics

First fix attempt (adding onlyBuiltDependencies) was already in the commit that failed CI — took multiple log-reading rounds to realize the lockfile lacked approval data and that the version mismatch was the real cause
Adding packageManager field caused a new CI error (conflict between packageManager and version input) because action-setup v6 rejects having both — required a second PR push
pnpm 11 turned out to be RC-only, making the 'just upgrade to pnpm 11' approach a dead end after workflow files were already edited
Multiple round-trips of reading, editing, then reverting workflow files across 5+ workflow yamls
open_items: PR #455 lint fix (version input removal from all workflow yaml files) was interrupted by the user before completion — the with: version: 10 blocks in all workflow files still need to be removed
